summary.overview: Chapter 4 explores the concept of a 'Green School' through an interactive dialogue between students Aasha and Mohit, who act as 'School Explorers' to transform their campus into a sustainable, safe, and joyful learning environment. The chapter defines a Green School as an eco-friendly campus that prioritizes source waste management, resource conservation, energy efficiency, passive solar architecture, and nature cultivation under the Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya campaign. Central to the lesson is source waste segregation into wet waste (organic, biodegradable items like fruit peels, tea leaves, and leftover lunch scraps placed in green bins for natural composting) and dry waste (non-biodegradable recyclables like paper, plastic, metal, and glass placed in blue bins). The text highlights the dignity, health, and safety of informal recyclers (kabadiwalas) and municipal sanitation workers, demonstrating how source segregation protects workers from glass cuts and prevents wet organic rot from ruining dry recyclable paper. It analyzes passive cooling mechanics, explaining how painting building roofs with high-albedo white reflective paint reflects shortwave solar radiation to cool classroom interiors without high electricity usage. Additionally, it features a quantitative water leakage audit showing that a single tap dripping at 1 drop per second wastes over 4.32 liters of clean water daily, and outlines student-led rainwater harvesting soak pits and school composting gardens.
